records.bodyText:
A wind farm that could provide electricity for two million homes risks having “significant adverse effects” on the landscape and cultural heritage of Scottish islands, councillors have been told.
The report for Argyll and Bute Council urges the local authority to oppose the MachairWind development, proposed by ScottishPower Renewables.
The energy giant is hoping to install 91 turbines at 335-metres in height or 144 280-metre turbines in waters to the north-west of Islay and to the west of Colonsay on Scotland’s west coast.

records.title: Conservationists write postcard to every MSP warning of seabird deaths from wind farm
records.bodyText:
CONSERVATIONISTS have delivered postcards to every MSP at Holyrood warning them that a planned offshore wind farm could kill 4,000 seabirds every year.
The Scottish Seabird Centre in North Berwick is warning that the Berwick Bank development could threaten thousands of seabirds each year.
The charity has delivered 129 handwritten postcards, one for every MSP, to the Scottish Parliament.
Fanny Royanez, policy and campaigns officer at the Seabird Centre, said: "These postcards and the sand art they display will be a powerful reminder to MSPs, as they come back from their summer recess, of the public opposition to Berwick Bank.

records.title: The ever increasing cost of ideology. Please read the full article 🙏
records.bodyText:
The ever increasing cost of ideology. Please read the full article 🙏
#AffordableEnergy #climatechange #Hopetosaveourcountryside
This did not happen by accident.
For nearly two decades, successive governments have pushed the same energy ideology: legally binding carbon targets, mass electrification, weather-dependent generation and a vast rebuild of the electricity grid — all sold to us on the promise of cheaper energy, green jobs and greater security.
Now look at the results.
Household energy debt is approaching £5 billion. Food prices are almost 40% higher than in 2020. Britain has some of the highest industrial electricity prices in the developed world. Energy-intensive industrial output has fallen by a third. Historic factories are closing, investment has gone overseas, and more of the goods we once made ourselves are being imported.
At the same time, the grid needed to support this transformation is running years behind the political timetable. Scotland is already showing what happens when renewable generation outruns transmission capacity: wind farms are being constrained because the electricity cannot always be moved to where it is needed, while consumers pick up the cost.
And after all this investment, Britain still needs tens of gigawatts of gas-fired generation to keep the system secure when the weather does not cooperate.
This is the story behind the montage.
Different politicians. Different governments. The same direction of travel.
The target came first. Engineering, affordability and industrial competitiveness came afterwards.
Now Britain is paying the price.
Read the full investigation here:
A MONTAGE OF FAILED IDEOLOGY — Britain was promised a green industrial revolution. What we got was higher bills, lost industry and a grid struggling to keep up.

records.title: SC Charollais
records.bodyText:
SC Charollais
Just look at the map....a bit OTT  !! Scotland been properly succored  !!
Wind Energy's Absurd
The National Audit Office has now published its examination of Britain's grid upgrade programme.
And there is rather more to it than the headlines about a £70bn upgrade and rising constraint payments.
The NAO's starting point is remarkably clear: renewable generation was allowed to expand faster than the transmission network, with successive governments' 'connect and manage' policy allowing generation to connect before the network was ready.  (How many times we've mentioned SCAM - Stop Connect And Manage!
But the report also asks some much more uncomfortable questions.
Why were opportunities to upgrade the grid earlier missed?
Why did Ofgem reject some proposed upgrades when they were first put forward, only for them subsequently to be approved at higher cost?
Why has there been no full whole-system business case or options appraisal for the grid upgrade programme, despite the costs ultimately being borne through consumers' bills?
And who, exactly, is accountable for the £70bn programme as a whole?
The NAO says there is currently no single person or organisation accountable for the overall progress and value for money of the portfolio.
Perhaps the most revealing illustration of how much the electricity system has changed is the NAO's own map comparing generation sites in 2000 with those operating in 2025.
In 2000 there were 179 major generation sites.
By 2025 there were 1,317.
The geography of electricity generation has been transformed.
The question is not whether the grid has to change with it.
The question is whether government, regulators and the industry planned that transformation properly - and whether consumers are now paying for the consequences of getting the sequencing wrong.

records.bodyText:
What are your thoughts on affordable energy vs. preserving the countryside?
Summarised by AI from the post below
NET ZERO The Government’s control
Which would you prefer?
#AffordableEnergy #climatechange #Hopetosaveourcountryside
NET ZERO The Government’s control
THE GREAT NET ZERO LAND CONTRADICTION
Why are we industrialising the countryside before we have exhausted the land we have already developed?
Britain has vast areas of warehouse roofs, factories, supermarkets, public buildings and car parks where solar power could be generated without sacrificing another field or transforming another rural community.
Yet enormous countryside developments—complete with fencing, access roads, inverter stations, substations, cables and battery compounds—continue to be presented as a national necessity.
If rooftop and car-park solar costs more, takes longer or is less attractive to investors, the Government should be honest about it. Communities should not be told there is no alternative simply because hundreds of acres of countryside are easier and more profitable to develop than thousands of separate roofs.
The cheapest project for a developer may become one of the costliest decisions Britain makes—for our countryside, food security and the communities left surrounded by industrial infrastructure for decades.
My latest article asks the simple question Ed Miliband and DESNZ must answer:
Why is inconvenience allowed to protect an already-developed car park, while “national necessity” is used to justify sacrificing the countryside?
Please read and share:
#SaveOurCountryside #SolarFarms #NetZero #FoodSecurity #ProtectOurFarmland

records.bodyText: Text reads: How to resist a data centre. What action can we take to stop new data centres in Scotland, and what might we learn from data centre resistance in the US and around the world? Part of Scotland Resists Big Tech Power. Saturday 13 June 2026, 11am to 4pm. Augustine United Church, Edinburgh, EH1 1EL. Free event (donations welcome). Speakers: Rachael Revesz (journalist and campaigner, chair); Ariane Burgess MSP (Green MSP for Highlands and Islands); Cllr Ben Parker (Green councillor for Morningside); Sarah Jaffe (US writer and reporter). Global Justice Now.
